context.objective: Document how we carry out Capital Call & Distribution Event Execution, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: It starts when a client tells us, or we identify, a need to move capital: a line of credit repayment, investment funding, a management fee, operating expenses, portfolio company proceeds or an ad hoc request. Let me walk the whole thing end to end. Step 1, the assigned preparer (CAP Activity Team or Fund Team, it depends on the event and client) opens the event: classifies it as a capital call, distribution or combined net event, records driver, entity, amount and expected cash dates, and names the preparer and second reviewer. Step 2, the preparer builds the event calendar from the LPA notice rule (business or calendar days) and checks bank holidays and payment cut-offs; if a requested date cannot meet the notice rule or cut-off we escalate. Step 3, the preparer assembles the data pack and marks every input final, estimated or pending. Step 4, the preparer copies the prior locked Excel event file forward, pulls beginning balances from the power report, trial balance and partner capital files and ties them to the prior deliverable; an unexplained difference is escalated to the reviewer and client before calculations are finalized. Step 5, preparer with reviewer and client freezes the methodology; if LPA treatment is ambiguous we pause and get written client or legal direction. Step 6, population gate: preparer lists every investor, reviewer checks independently; any unconfirmed change stays excluded until written client direction. Step 7, preparer runs the allocations in Excel and fills the summary allocation tab; investor totals must equal fund totals apart from documented rounding. Step 8, preparer reconciles to partner capital, GP unfunded and trial balance, reviewer verifies; any unexplained difference pauses client submission. Step 9, the second reviewer does the internal review; comments go back to the preparer for correction, otherwise sign-off. Step 10, preparer sends the package to the client; feedback means we revise and repeat affected checks; on final written approval we lock the file. No posting or release before that. Step 11, preparer merges notices from the summary tab into the Word template, converts to PDF, and the reviewer compares each notice to the locked allocation in e-check; failures are regenerated, never patched. Step 12, Fund Team or preparer prepares journal entries, routes them through accounting review and posts in the GL (Allvue or Entrilia); for cash outflows Treasury initiates payment after bank detail controls. Step 13, Investor Services splits notices, uploads to the investor portal and releases the email campaign, holding release on any mapping or contact discrepancy. Step 14, closeout: for a call we hand the receivable baseline to receipt tracking; for a distribution we confirm wires settled; update historical records, complete client deliverables and retain the final package.
Who is accountable for the overall result across these event steps?

I do not know. The overall process owner and the internal approver have not been confirmed, and ownership between the CAP Activity Team and the Fund Team is not standardized. What I can say is that the preparing team and a second reviewer from the assigned operating team must be named when the event opens, the second reviewer must sign off before anything goes to the client, and the client approves the final event amounts and notices. The exact role title of the second reviewer is also not confirmed.
What determines how the event amount is allocated across investors in the Excel file?

Money moves on this work, so investors could be asked to fund the wrong amounts by a due date or be paid the wrong proceeds. The specific failures we guard against are: the event run for the wrong investor population, which means the event has failed even if the math is right; a notice that does not agree with the locked allocation; a missed manual notice step that discloses information to the wrong party or releases inconsistent notices; a due date that breaks the LPA notice rule or lands on a bank holiday or past a cut-off so it cannot be executed; and a posted GL entry that does not equal the locked totals. If an error or a late client change is found after posting, the entry has to be reversed and reposted through the controlled accounting workflow, and the affected review, notice and approval steps are repeated. Errors also flow downstream into receipt tracking for calls, distribution economics and Treasury execution.
Roughly how many capital call, distribution, or combined net events does the team handle in a typical month?

I cannot give you a measured breakdown of where the time goes, nobody has estimated that. What I can say: setup and inputs are manual and depend on client instructions. Allocation rules and percentages live in Excel, and every event starts by copying the prior workbook forward and tying beginning balances to the prior deliverable; the workbook can carry manual entries, plugs, manual rounding, hidden tabs, broken links and outdated settings that have to be sourced or cleaned up. Historical proceeds, tax details and special rules can be spread across several workpapers. Rework mainly comes from repeated client changes, which make version control harder, and from changes after posting, which force a reversal and repost with renewed approvals. Investor Services also has to split notices manually and coordinate the email campaign. As a rough example only, a basic capital call takes a couple of hours, while a complex distribution with holdbacks, tranches, waterfall or tax coordination can take a couple of days or longer.
About how many capital call, distribution, or combined net events do you handle in a typical month?

Several things. For One Rock we complete a Cobalt upload within two days of a capital event, at closeout. GP vehicles have their own population, waiver, commitment and carry rules. Deal-by-deal or tranche-based funds keep separate allocation history per investment or tranche. For net events we keep the call and distribution components separate even when the investor sees one net amount. Notice timing varies by fund: some LPAs use business days, some calendar days, and they are not interchangeable. Where the governing documents are silent on an allocation treatment, we only use a written, current client-approved methodology for that specific fund. Clients can also elect the narrative, notice date, presentation, net-event display or recipient population, and that is recorded in the event brief. The GL platform and journal entry approval route differ by entity, Allvue or Entrilia, but which entity uses which is not confirmed. And when we also service the management company, invoice information comes from that team as well as the Fund Team. Nothing differs by country or currency that I know of.
For a combined net event, what happens at closeout for its call and distribution components?
This capture still has open sections. 12 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.

steps.description: Build the calendar using the LPA notice rule, including whether it uses business or calendar days. Check bank holidays and payment cut-offs; escalate if the requested date cannot meet the rule or cut-off.
steps.handoff: Escalation recipient and resolution are UNKNOWN
steps.input: Event dates and LPA notice rule
steps.rule_source_ref: LPA, as reported by participant; document not reviewed
steps.title: Build event calendar

steps.completion_criteria: Every input marked final, estimated or pending
steps.data_origin: Client instructions; applicable management company and Fund Team invoice information; other sources UNKNOWN
steps.description: Assemble the event inputs and mark each final, estimated or pending. Where GPFS also services the management company, invoice information comes from that team as well as the Fund Team.
steps.handoff: Preparer uses the pack for the event file
steps.input: Event inputs and applicable client instructions

operating_details.text: Historical proceeds, tax details and special rules can be spread across several workpapers.

steps.title: Assemble data pack

steps.completion_criteria: Balances tied or unexplained differences escalated
steps.data_origin: Prior event file, power report, trial balance and partner capital files
steps.description: Copy the prior locked event file forward, pull beginning balances from the power report, trial balance and partner capital files, and tie them to the prior deliverable. Escalate unexplained differences to the reviewer and client before calculations are finalized.
steps.handoff: Reviewer and client receive unexplained differences
steps.input: Prior locked event file, power report, trial balance, partner capital files and prior deliverable
steps.output: Carried-forward file and tied beginning balances
steps.title: Carry forward and tie balances

steps.completion_criteria: Methodology frozen; ambiguity addressed with written direction
steps.data_origin: Reported LPA treatment and client or legal direction where needed
steps.description: Freeze the methodology together. If LPA treatment is ambiguous, pause for written client or legal direction; where governing documents are silent, use only a written, current client-approved methodology for that fund.
steps.handoff: Frozen methodology supports population and allocation work
steps.input: Event methodology and applicable governing-document treatment
steps.output: Frozen methodology and applicable written direction
steps.rule_source_ref: LPA and client-approved methodology as reported; documents not reviewed
steps.title: Freeze methodology

steps.completion_criteria: Independent check completed; unconfirmed changes excluded pending written client direction
steps.data_origin: Investor population source UNKNOWN
steps.description: The preparer lists every investor and the reviewer checks independently. An unconfirmed change stays excluded until written client direction.
steps.handoff: Checked population used for allocations
steps.input: Investor population and proposed changes
steps.title: Check investor population

steps.completion_criteria: Investor totals equal fund totals apart from documented rounding
steps.data_origin: Event data pack and investor population; allocation rules and percentages in Excel
steps.description: Run allocations and fill the summary allocation tab; investor totals must equal fund totals apart from documented rounding. Keep call and distribution components separate for net events, and separate allocation history by investment or tranche for applicable funds; GP vehicles have their own population, waiver, commitment and carry rules.
steps.handoff: Preparer reconciles allocations
steps.input: Event inputs, frozen methodology and checked investor population
steps.rule_source_ref: Methodology frozen by preparer, reviewer and client; detailed rule sources UNKNOWN
steps.title: Run allocations

steps.completion_criteria: Reviewer verification; unexplained differences hold client submission
steps.data_origin: Partner capital, GP unfunded and trial balance
steps.description: The preparer reconciles to partner capital, GP unfunded and the trial balance, and the reviewer verifies. An unexplained difference pauses client submission.
steps.handoff: Event proceeds to internal review
steps.input: Allocations, partner capital, GP unfunded and trial balance
steps.title: Reconcile allocations

steps.completion_criteria: Internal sign-off
steps.data_origin: Prepared event package
steps.description: The second reviewer performs internal review. Comments return to the preparer for correction; the reviewer must sign off before the package goes to the client.
steps.handoff: Comments go to preparer; signed-off package proceeds to client
steps.input: Event package and reconciliations
steps.title: Complete internal review

steps.completion_criteria: Written approval received and file locked
steps.data_origin: Client feedback and approval
steps.description: Send the package to the client, revise for feedback and repeat affected checks. The client approves final event amounts and notices; on final written approval, lock the file. No posting or release occurs before that approval.
steps.handoff: Approved locked allocations support notices and subsequent posting
steps.input: Internally reviewed package
steps.output: Final written client approval and locked file
steps.title: Obtain client approval

steps.completion_criteria: Each notice compared to locked allocation; failures regenerated
steps.data_origin: Locked allocation file
steps.description: Merge notices from the summary tab into the Word template and convert them to PDF. The reviewer compares each notice to the locked allocation in e-check; failed notices are regenerated, not patched.
steps.handoff: Notices proceed toward Investor Services release
steps.input: Locked summary allocation tab and Word template
steps.title: Prepare and check notices

steps.actor: Fund Team or preparer; accounting reviewer; Treasury for cash outflows
steps.completion_criteria: Accounting review and posting completed; bank detail controls precede payment initiation
steps.data_origin: Approved event and bank details; detailed sources UNKNOWN
steps.description: The Fund Team or preparer prepares journal entries, routes them through accounting review and posts them in the GL. For cash outflows, Treasury initiates payment after bank detail controls; the GL platform and approval route differ by entity.
steps.handoff: Treasury initiates applicable cash outflows
steps.input: Approved event; bank details for cash outflows
steps.output: Posted journal entries and, where applicable, initiated payments
steps.title: Post entries and initiate payments

steps.completion_criteria: Investor portal upload and email release completed with no mapping or contact discrepancy
steps.data_origin: Checked notices; mapping and contact sources UNKNOWN
steps.description: Manually split notices, upload them to the investor portal and release the email campaign. Hold release for any mapping or contact discrepancy.
steps.handoff: Only discrepancy-free notice release proceeds to closeout; discrepancy resolution and resume path are UNKNOWN
steps.input: Checked notices and investor mapping and contact information

operating_details.text: holding release on any mapping or contact discrepancy.

steps.output: Portal notices and released email campaign
steps.title: Release investor notices

steps.completion_criteria: Applicable handoff or settlement confirmed, records updated, deliverables completed and package retained
steps.data_origin: Event records and settlement information
steps.description: For a call, hand the receivable baseline to receipt tracking; for a distribution, confirm wires settled. Update historical records, complete client deliverables and retain the final package. For One Rock, complete a Cobalt upload within two days of a capital event, at closeout.
steps.handoff: Receivable baseline to receipt tracking for a call
steps.input: Event records, receivable baseline or wire settlement information

operating_details.text: within two days of a capital event, at closeout.

steps.output: Updated history, completed deliverables and retained final package
steps.rule_source_ref: One Rock closeout requirement as reported; source UNKNOWN
steps.system: Cobalt for One Rock upload; other systems UNKNOWN
steps.title: Close out event

steps.completion_criteria: Need to move capital identified or communicated
steps.data_origin: Client tells GPFS or GPFS identifies the need
steps.description: Work starts when a client tells GPFS, or GPFS identifies, a need to move capital, including a line of credit repayment, investment funding, management fee, operating expense, portfolio company proceeds or an ad hoc request.
steps.handoff: Assigned preparer opens the event
steps.input: UNKNOWN
steps.title: Need to move capital identified

steps.completion_criteria: Controlled reversal and reposting and affected steps repeated
steps.data_origin: Error or late client change found after posting
steps.description: If an error or late client change is found after posting, reverse and repost the entry through the controlled accounting workflow. Repeat affected review, notice and approval steps.
steps.handoff: Affected review, notice and approval steps; exact routes depend on the change
steps.input: Posted entry and identified error or late client change
steps.output: Reversed and reposted entry with affected checks and approvals repeated
steps.system: Controlled accounting workflow; specific system UNKNOWN
steps.title: Correct post-posting changes

workflow.title: Capital Call & Distribution Event Execution

actors: Assigned preparer: CAP Activity Team or Fund Team
Fund Team or preparer; accounting reviewer; Treasury for cash outflows
